thread.title: Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox lead Spurs' Game 2 rout
thread.title_full: Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox lead Spurs' Game 2 rout

author: Greg Luca, Rhyma Castillo, Staff Writers
title: Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox lead Spurs' Game 2 rout
text:
Erasing a letdown performance in the series opener, the Spurs cruised to a rout in Game 2 of their Western Conference semifinals series against the Timberwolves, winning 133-95 on Wednesday in the Frost Bank Center.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
The margin was just shy of the largest blowout in playoff history for the Spurs, chasing a 145-105 win against Denver in 1983.
Seven San Antonio players scored in double figures, complementing a stifling performance on the defensive end. The series is level at 1-1 entering Game 3 at 8:30 p.m. Friday in Minnesota.
Greg Luca
With Victor Wembanyama and the rest of the starters watching from the bench, the Spurs reserves continue to extend the lead. Harrison Barnes has nine points, scoring on back-to-back possessions as San Antonio pushed the margin to 44 points.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Greg Luca
The Spurs’ Game 1 loss ended with Julian Champagnie misfiring on a 3-point attempt from the right wing. But Champagnie hasn’t let one missed opportunity haunt him in Game 2, knocking down all four 3-point attempts on the way to 12 points in the third quarter.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
With suffocating defense and all five starters scoring in double figures, San Antonio continues to extend a massive lead, up 98-63 as the third quarter closes.
Greg Luca
After fouling out of Game 1, Spurs guard Stephon Castle has four fouls midway through the third quarter of Game 2. Castle has scored a game-high 19 points in 22 minutes on the court but will need to manage his typically physical defense down the stretch.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Keldon Johnson also has four fouls for San Antonio, while Jaden McDaniels and Terrence Shannon each have four for Minnesota. The teams were whistled for a combined 13 fouls in just more than seven minutes of third-quarter action.
The lulls haven’t stopped the Spurs from extending their lead, as back-to-back 3-pointers from Julian Champagnie pushed the margin to 30 late in the third quarter.
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Officials sent both teams to their benches to conduct an official review after a tussle between Stephon Castle and Bones Hyland following a jump ball.
Castle initially shoved Hyland as the two battled for position. Once Hyland recovered from a brief stumble, he walked over to Castle and shoved him toward midcourt, long after the Spurs had won possession. Both teams gathered around the potential scrum as the whistle blew and officials separated the two players.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Castle was assessed a loose ball foul, while Hyland earned a technical.
Greg Luca
Sports podcaster and NBA pundit Kevin O’Connor isn’t hemming and hawing in his appraisal of the Spurs’ performance so far in Game 2. “Pure dominance,” he calls it.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Pure dominance by the Spurs. My goodness what a defensive clinic.
— Kevin O'Connor (@KevinOConnor)[May 7, 2026]
Spurs guard Devin Vassell delivered a rarely seen alley-oop basket from beyond the arc during the third quarter, jumping before receiving the baseline pass from Julian Champagnie and burying the 3-pointer in one smooth motion.
Just like they drew it up 😏
— San Antonio Spurs (@spurs)
📺 ESPN[pic.twitter.com/SkckLtEeUP][May 7, 2026]
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Charles Barkley, the former NBA great turned commentator, is free with his opinions, and his opinion tonight is that the Timberwolves are showing some serious pluck by continuing to drive to the hoop, knowing that Victor Wembanyama will be waiting for them in the paint..
"If somebody blocked my damn shot 12 times, I'm not sure I'm gonna keep going in there."
— NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA)
Chuck gives the Timberwolves credit for continuing to drive in the lane 🤝[pic.twitter.com/jxmzEPQRHS][May 6, 2026]
San Antonio author and humorist Shea Serrano can’t get enough of how the Jackals, the Spurs’ official cheer squad, have raised their game for round two of the Spurs’ playoff push.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
“Ayyyyyye, this is so dope. the jackals are basically turning spurs games into soccer games were like two weeks away from in-arena smoke flares lol,” Serrano wrote on X.
ayyyyyye this is so dope — the jackals are basically turning spurs games into soccer games were like two weeks away from in-arena smoke flares lol — shoutout the homie eugene from
— Shea Serrano (@SheaSerrano)[@ledger]for the assist 🙌🏼🙌🏼🙌🏼🙌🏼🙌🏼[pic.twitter.com/Wh7LG2j6Tc][May 7, 2026]
After combining for a disappointing 21 points in a Game 1 loss, Spurs stars Victor Wembanyama and De’Aaron Fox have carried the offensive load in Game 2, totaling 28 points in the opening half as San Antonio charged to a dominating 59-35 lead.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
San Antonio’s two leading scorers during the regular season, Wembanyama and Fox were a combined 0 for 12 from 3-point range in the series opener but connected on 3 of 4 from outside to open action Wednesday, complementing their relentless attack on the pick and roll.
And when Fox and Wembanyama both went to the bench late in the first half, the Spurs continued to surge, scoring 11 points in a stretch of less than two minutes as San Antonio stretched the margin into blowout territory.
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
San Antonio Spurs superfans, the Jackals, brought playoff energy to another level ahead of the team’s pivotal matchup against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Inside the Frost Bank Center, the group unveiled its first-ever “tifo” — a massive choreographed fan display stretching across the bleachers at Frost Bank Center. Held high by dozens of fans, the banner delivered a bold message to the crowd and team alike: “Built to win together.”
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Rhyma Castillo
During a brief break in game action, a Spurs fan seated courtside sent a breeze Rudy Gobert’s way using a fan with Keldon Johnson’s face on it. Sports journalist Jared Weiss captured the moment.
lol at this lady fanning Rudy Gobert with Keldon Johnson’s face
— Jared Weiss (@JaredWeissNBA)[pic.twitter.com/2wqCk8chdr][May 7, 2026]
With four free throws from Stephon Castle to cap a run of five straight points, San Antonio built an 11-point lead early in the second quarter, marking the largest margin either side has built early in the series.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
In such a physical, defensive-focused matchup, leads of that size will likely be hard to come by.
Greg Luca
Finding his stride on offense after a slow start in San Antonio’s second-round series, Spurs star Victor Wembanyama has 11 early points in Game 2.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Wembanyama opened with a follow-up slam off a missed 3-pointer, then tapped in a layup through a foul off a feed from Devin Vassell.
He added two more baskets in the opening minutes of the second quarter, converting from close range and then putting back his own miss.
COUNT THAT ☝️
— San Antonio Spurs (@spurs)
📺 ESPN[pic.twitter.com/9vit9C9tVj][May 7, 2026]
Greg Luca
The Spurs and Timberwolves are living up to the billing as a series focused on defense first, with the teams combining to miss their first 12 attempts from 3-point range during the opening quarter.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
San Antonio has a 24-17 lead behind 16 combined points from De’Aaron Fox and Victor Wembanyama, who have attacked off the pick-and-roll to break out of an offensive slump in Game 1.
The Timberwolves and Spurs both started 0 for 6 from beyond the arc before Anthony Edwards connected for Minnesota and Fox answered by rattling one home for San Antonio during the final minute of the opening period.
Nine minutes in, the Spurs and Timberwolves are combining to tie Wilt Chamberlain’s NBA record for fewest 3-pointers in a game.
— Mike Finger ([@mikefinger.bsky.social])[May 6, 2026 at 9:07 PM]
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
After combining for 21 points in a Game 1 loss, De’Aaron Fox and Victor Wembanyama have found their scoring touch to open Game 2, combining to produce the Spurs’ first 11 points.
The duo has combined to hit five of their first six shots.
After combining for 21 points in all of Game 1, Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox have combined for the Spurs' first 11 tonight.
— Jeff McDonald (@JMcDonald_SAEN)[May 7, 2026]
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
After saying his energy was focused too much on defense instead of offense in Game 1, Victor Wembenyama jumped out to a strong start in Game 2, crashing in for a thunderous follow-up dunk in the opening minutes.
Wembanyama set an NBA record for a playoff game with 12 blocks as part of a triple-double on Monday, but he finished with just 11 points. He needed only about four minutes to score his first seven points Wednesday.
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
A video posted to the Minnesota Timberwolves’ official X account shortly before the game showed T-Wolves center Rudy Gobert receiving a quick, sportsmanlike hug from his Spurs counterpart and fellow Frenchman, Victor Wembanyama, on the side of the court.
Nothing surprising there. But once Wemby had jogged off, Gobert – still seated courtside in a folding chair – tossed up a 3-ball. Nothing but net.
🥶🥶🥶
— Minnesota Timberwolves (@Timberwolves)[pic.twitter.com/2wAeLeOr6A][May 7, 2026]
Tipoff between the Spurs and Timberwolves appears to be running behind the scheduled 8:30 p.m. start time. No official reason has been announced yet. But the Knicks vs. Philadelphia is running long.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
The smell of fresh pan dulce could soon mix with the sounds of honking horns and “Go Spurs Go” chants in downtown San Antonio. As the San Antonio Spurs prepare for Wednesday night’s playoff game against the Minnesota Timberwolves, Alamo Biscuit Company & Panadería is betting on a win and baking hundreds of conchas to celebrate it.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
If the Spurs beat the Timberwolves, the restaurant plans to hand out 500 free conchas to fans driving down Commerce Street as part of what organizers are calling the city’s "Spurs Victory Thoroughfare."
Trey Lopez
The San Antonio Spurs are once again facing off against the Minnesota Timberwolves in the second round of the NBA playoffs tonight, and they're coming back to the home court in casual yet stylish attire. Here's what they were wearing when they arrived for the occasion.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Rhyma Castillo
After Minnesota coach Chris Finch suggested in media interviews Tuesday that at least four of Victor Wembanyama’s blocks from Monday could have been called goaltends, San Antonio coach Mitch Johnson brushed off the concern before tipoff of Game 2.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Wembanyama blocked 12 shots in Monday’s loss as part of a triple-double, setting the NBA record for blocks in a postseason game.
San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson, on Minnesota’s claims that some of Victor Wembanyama’s 12 blocks in Game 1 should have been called goaltending: “There's a lot of uncalled plays in the game. I didn’t go back and keep track of all of them or take note of all of them.”
— Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation)[pic.twitter.com/tZsrrEaBra][May 6, 2026]
Greg Luca
Guard Carter Bryant told reporters shortly before tipoff Wednesday that he’ll be available to play in Game 2, and the Spurs made it official a few minutes later, listing Bryant as “available” on the team’s injury report.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
The 20-year-old rookie sat out Monday’s game due to a right foot sprain suffered in practice and was previously listed as questionable. He appeared off the bench in all five games of the Spurs’ first-round series against Portland but was held to six minutes or less in three of them.
Carter Bryant told reporters he will be available tonight, but there’s nothing official yet from the Spurs.
— Tom Orsborn (@tom_orsborn)[May 7, 2026]
Greg Luca
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Two San Antonio Spurs legends made an appearance at the Frost Bank Center ahead of the team’s Game 2 against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday night.
The event stemmed from a partnership between the Spurs and USAA to provide game tickets and a special “chalk talk” meet-and-greet with Sean Elliott and Bruce Bowen for 50 U.S. service members stationed in San Antonio, according to a Wednesday news release.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Rhyma Castillo
Minnesota coach Chris Finch said shortly before Wednesday’s tipoff that star Anthony Edwards is in line to “play a few more minutes” after logging 25 in his surprising return from a knee injury during Monday’s Game 1 win.
Guard Ayo Dosunmu, who has missed the past two games due to a right calf strain, is also stepping back into action in Game 2. He averaged 14.4 points per game during the regular season after being traded to Minnesota but exploded for 43 in a Game 4 win against Denver during the opening round, becoming one of the most talked-about players in the league.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
Greg Luca
After neither team led by more than nine points during Minnesota’s 104-102 win during Game 1, San Antonio has been installed as a 10.5-point betting favorite in Game 2.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
The Spurs were also a 10.5-point favorite in Game 1, only to be upset on their home court, meeting the type of fight from the Timberwolves that is typical for a playoff atmosphere. But Las Vegas rakes in money for a reason. San Antonio was 32-8 at home during the regular season, and the Spurs were 5.3 points per 100 possessions better than the Timberwolves over the course of the year.
Vegas usually isn't wrong, especially twice in a row but ...
— Jeff McDonald (@JMcDonald_SAEN)
I really don't understand this spread at all.[https://t.co/lgYGhujX1N][May 6, 2026]
Greg Luca
After Victor Wembanyama and De’Aaron Fox delivered an offensive dud in Game 1, all eyes will be on San Antonio’s two leading scorers as they look to bounce back in Game 2.
Advertisement
Article continues below this ad
The Spurs duo combined for less than half of their regular season average with 21 points and nine turnovers in Monday’s loss, missing all 12 shots from beyond the arc. Their chance for redemption in Game 2 arrives at 8:30 p.m. at the Frost Bank Center, airing on ESPN.
Greg Luca
